gaps.note: The page's definitions (Gram matrix invertible, dimension product, F of dimension h) need finite dimension, and the paper (line 856, F=Q^h, line 877 dimension m) uses finite-dimensional spaces. Countable dimension is wrong or unsupported: the invertible-Gram-matrix definition of nondegeneracy does not make sense for infinite dimensions. It should say finite dimensions.

The page never states that tensoring distributes over the orthogonal sum, nor that B tensor C and P tensor C are orthogonal and span A tensor C under the product form. The reader, new to tensor products, is not shown this identity (paper lines 939-944 use it without proof).
